name: painting_deep
note: A drawn painting at deep: two lights as rivals, the critique naming one craft decision.

thoughts.text: A woman in her fifties, calm, her hair windblown, in a lilac robe, resting.
A cathedral at noon. She holds a candle that sits below a window, so daylight and flame share the same stretch of wall.
Light comes from below, from the candle in her hands: it lifts the chin and the folds of the robe. Against noon at the window, the flame is a small, warm rival.
The lilac robe, lit from below by flame, warms toward rose and becomes the picture's soft centre.
Portrait framing, close and vertical, with the window above the candle drawing the eye up and the flame pulling it back down.
Awed, but quietly: the calm face and the resting pose keep it from drama, and the cathedral does the work of scale.
Windblown hair indoors is the odd detail. It suggests an open door or a draught, so even the stone room is not entirely still.
A devotional piece for a family: something to keep in a home, calm enough to live with, grand enough to feel sacred.
A farewell, with the last prayer already said: the candle is what she carries out of the room.
At night the window would go dark and the candle would be the only world. At noon it is one light among two, and she is choosing which to follow.

wordings.text: A woman in her fifties with windblown hair and a calm face rests in a lilac robe, holding a candle below a cathedral window at noon, lit from below.

Lighting the face from the flame, in a room full of noon, is a lovely reversal, and the lilac holds the warmth well. The window above the candle is a little too bright; dim it so the flame, not the glass, gets the last word.
